A column product's tiles are of its own encoding (`values.encoding`) and carry no `dbz`. With `products=nowcast`, meteocool's own nowcast (experimental): `nowcast_ch`, `nowcast_fr`, `nowcast_cz` and `nowcast_pl`, each that network's newest complete run issued in the last 30 minutes, its steps keyed by the step they are valid at and shaped as WN's are in `frames` (`source` `nowcast_phys`, tiles in the nowcast bucket, `upstream_time` the run's issue time); with `lat`, `lon` and `network`, that network's steps carry `dbz` at the point. A network without a fresh run is absent; Germany has none here. Empty unless asked for.

info.description:
Welcome to the meteocool backend. You are free to use our raw and aggregated
data for your private and server applications. If you are planning on releasing
a publicly available application, please cache these endpoints on your side
rather than having your users hit them directly.

## Compatibility

We cannot guarantee consistency or availability of these endpoints, but `/v3/`
endpoints will not introduce breaking changes soon. Most are rate limited,
especially on error responses.

## Attributions

Always attribute the original data sources. You, not us, are responsible to the
copyright holders if you fail to.

* Radar, precipitation types and nowcast data: **DWD**
* Radar outside Germany: the network that measured it, **MeteoSwiss**,
  **Météo-France**, **ČHMÚ**, **IMGW-PIB**, **RMI** and **VMM** (Belgium),
  **SHMÚ**
* Lightning data: **blitzortung.org**

We would appreciate an attribution to meteocool too.

## Mobile endpoints

Endpoints tagged `mobile` are documented for completeness; they need a valid
APNS or Firebase push token and are write-only, because the read channel is the
notification delivered to the device.

Per-minute strike counts inside a polygon, for the last half hour.

put.description:
Store each commute, and forget the token's commutes not in the list.

Before each scheduled departure, from `lead` minutes before it, every
run of the domain the commute starts in reads the way for the departures
within `flexibility` of it, and alerts once if leaving on time is wet. A
commute sent again keeps what it was alerted for, so a changed name or
route does not alert the same departure twice. An empty list forgets
every commute.

get.description:
The chart at a point, read by the domain the map draws there, as its alerts are.

`/v3/radar/timeseries` reads DWD's unless the client names a network,
which an app cannot know: in Paris or Warsaw it charts nothing while the
alerts come from that network's run. Here the point's domain decides,
and the series is that domain's: a network's composites and its own
nowcast, or DWD's HX and WN. `threshold`, `lang` and `details` add the
headlines and words as the timeseries does. Only with a push token in
`X-Push-Token`, within its quota.

post.description:
Replace what is stored of a registered phone's rain Live Activity.

Its own route rather than fields on `/location`, whose model forbids
unknown fields. `la_started` is left alone while the activity stays on:
a phone that swiped this rain's activity away sends no activity token,
and must not be sent another start for the same rain. Switching it on
asks for one, so it is forgotten then.

A phone that can start an activity now and could not before is decided
for at once: rain already due starts it without waiting for the next run.

The activity is the phone's own location's, or with `place` one of its
saved places' (Better Rain Alarm), each its own, started with that place
in its attributes. A place's is started by the next run, not at once.

put.description:
Store each place as a push client of its own, and forget the token's places not in the list.

A place is then decided, alerted and cleared exactly as a phone's location
is, by the run of the domain it is in, with flags of its own; its alerts'
titles start with its name, and carry its id as `place`. A place sent
again keeps its flags, so an alert it is showing is not sent again. An
empty list forgets every place; the phone's location and commutes stay.
`pausedUntil` is set on the phone's location too.

400.description: A token the push provider says is dead.

put.summary: Replace the places a phone wants alerts for.

post.description:
Where the traveller is at each moment of the trip, and how wet that gets them, by departure.

The way is read about every kilometre (at most 60 points), each point
passed at its fraction of `duration`, from the same radar series
`/v3/radar/timeseries` charts there: what was measured, then the
forecast, each network's own where the map draws that network. Each
departure says what each point reads in the five-minute step it is
passed in, and how many seconds of the trip are at or above
`threshold`; the advice says when to leave, and the headline says it
in words, in `lang`, with times for the device to fill in.

Without `departures`: from now, floored to five minutes, every five
minutes for as long as the trip still ends inside the forecast -- and
at least the first -- at most 48.

Only with a push token in `X-Push-Token`, within its quota, and a few
routes at a time: one waiting too long for its turn is answered 503.

get.description:
The newest Belgian reflectivity composite -- one frame, not a timeseries.

RMI's Jabbeke and Wideumont and VMM's Helchteren, composited by meteocool
from the lowest tilt of each volume; it reaches well into the Netherlands.
See `/switzerland` for why this is a route of its own.

The most recent precipitation-type tile set.

Served at /api/precip_types/ by the old Flask service, which this replaces.

The newest column maximum of every network -- one frame, not a timeseries.

DMAX's picture over every network on the map: the strongest echo above each cell
from every tilt of every radar, composited by meteocool once a cycle on a
background worker, with the networks evened out where they can be -- one
five-minute cycle, 180 km from any radar, up to 12 km, nothing under 12
dBZ. Stamped with its cycle, as DMAX is, and about seven minutes behind

get.description:
Each EUMETNET network's exclusive coverage, and what of it and its country is cut out of DWD's tiles.

Inside a network's own borders only that network draws; outside every
border the nearest radar that reaches does, whatever its network, DWD's
out to 150 km. The map clips each network's layer to its coverage and
holes DWD's tiles with the rest, and the server decides by the same
shapes which domain a point belongs to, so the two cannot
disagree. They change only with a release.

The newest Swiss reflectivity composite -- one frame, not a timeseries.

A route of its own beside `/timeseries`, which carries this network's
past too (`networks.ch`): a client refetches this whenever a radar reports
-- every minute or two, on the `network` socket event -- and the whole
timeseries only when DWD publishes. Same `RadarFrame` shape as every other
frame here, so the client needs one type and one tile-URL builder for
every network.

Tile metadata for each timestep in a window, past and forecast.

With `lat` and `lon`, each frame also carries the dBZ at that point. With
`network` as well, it is that network's reading wherever it has a composite
for the step -- which is every observed step, while its ingest is running
-- and DWD's everywhere else, the forecast included. The client names the
network because it is the one that knows which draws where, and a point
sampled from a network the map is not showing there would put bars under
the chart that nothing on the map agrees with.

`products` adds another observed product's frames for the same steps, for
a client drawing that one instead: DWD's column maximum, `dmax`, the
merged composite, `merged`, the column maximum of every network,
`colmax`, or one of that pass's column products: an echo top,
`echotop18`, `echotop45` or `echotop50`, or `vil`. Asked for rather than
always sent, since each frame carries its tile index and most clients
draw none of them. The chart is still read from HX and the networks,
whichever is drawn; a column product's frames carry no reading.

`products=nowcast` adds meteocool's own nowcast: each network's
newest complete run, under `nowcast_<domain>`, its steps keyed by the
forecast steps they are valid at, shaped as WN's are in `frames`. With a
point and `network`, that network's steps carry the dBZ there, and the
`headlines` are worded from them instead of WN's, up to the run's last
lead. Germany's run is never served: WN is Germany's forecast.

`threshold`, the dBZ the client counts as rain, adds what the chart comes
to in words, `headlines`, in `lang`, with the peak's dBZ when `details`:
the same words and rules as the rain alerts and Live Activities, so that
the apps show text rather than work it out.

The newest vertically integrated liquid of every network -- one frame, not a timeseries.

The liquid water in each cell's column, kg m⁻², by Greene and Clark from
the tilts the column maximum of every network is built from, once a cycle
and stamped with it. Its tiles are `vil-0.5kg-u8`. Refetched on
the `network` socket event (`vil`); its past is in `/timeseries` when asked
for (`products=vil`).
